title: Statistical safety net and canary gating for quantized stacks
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Add a statistical gating layer and automatic fallback mechanism for quantized model rollouts. The feature will integrate with the existing canary runner to validate FP8/INT8 calibration profiles against production-like prompt slices and automatically route traffic back to a high-precision variant when accuracy regressions exceed predefined thresholds.
background: We have accelerating adoption of INT8/FP8 deployment profiles to reduce per-token cost, but several recent small-scale rollouts exposed subtle quality regressions on low-frequency slices (e.g., long-context summarization, math expressions, and code completion). Manual rollbacks are slow; we need an automated safety net that balances rollout velocity against statistical confidence in regressions.
approach: 1) Instrument canary runner to collect per-request golden-pair metrics (reference output scoring via eval harness) and lightweight signal probes (e.g., log-likelihood delta, token-level perplexity, semantic embedding cosine with gold). 2) Apply sequential hypothesis testing (SPRT) + Bayesian A/B checks on streaming results to stop and rollback early. 3) Implement traffic steering rules to fall back to a tagged high-precision variant (FP32/quant-safe) with zero-downtime.
calibration_workflow: Calibration job produces profile artifacts (scale/zero params, per-layer histograms) and an associated calibration-report hash stored in S3. For canaries we will run the calibration job on a held-out calibration set and produce a 'calibration confidence score' computed from slice-level distribution shifts and layer-wise activation KL divergence. The harness will reject profiles whose confidence score < 0.85.
validation_plan: Validation uses three tiers: 1) Fast synthetics (1000 prompts) to catch gross regressions, 2) Production slices (10k prompts sampled over target traffic) for SLO-grade checks, 3) Offline regression checks on curated hard prompts (200 examples) for semantic correctness. Metrics: semantic-ROUGE (or embedding cosine), token-error-rate for structured outputs, and latency p95. Define per-metric thresholds and an aggregate composite score.
canary_strategy: Canary is staged in 4 steps: 0.0% -> 0.5% -> 5% -> 20% over a configurable window (default window=30m per step). At each step the SPRT accumulates evidence; thresholds tuned to bound Type I error < 1% and Type II error < 10% for the composite score. If SPRT accepts alternative hypothesis (regression) at any point, traffic is immediately steered to fallback variant and an incident event is emitted.
fallback_policy: Fallback targets a model tag defined in the deployment config (e.g., model:my-model@fp32-stable). The policy is: immediate rollback of new variant traffic, preserve existing inflight KV caches for the stable variant where compatible, and mark the quantized profile as 'rejected' with a reason code. A background job re-runs calibration with adjusted quant params and queues a re-eval before any reattempt.
monitoring: Expose real-time canary dashboards: composite score timeseries, SPRT statistic, slice-level deltas, and traffic ramp state. Hook alerts to PagerDuty when: a) SPRT triggers rollback, b) composite score drops > 5 sigma from baseline, or c) p95 latency regresses beyond SLA. Store canary traces and per-token diagnostics in the observability store for 7d by default.
tradeoffs_and_risks:
- Aggressive thresholds reduce rollout speed and increase developer friction; conservative thresholds risk user-facing regressions.
- SPRT requires independent samples; traffic autocorrelation may inflate false alarms. We'll mitigate with stratified sampling and minibatching.
- Maintaining compatibility of KV caches across precision variants is non-trivial; safe fallback may require cache flushes which impact short-term latency.
acceptance_criteria: Canary runner emits per-request composite score and SPRT statistic to telemetry in prod staging
Automated rollback triggers and routes traffic to a tagged fallback model within 30s of SPRT decision
Calibration confidence score computed and enforced during canary admission
Dashboards and alerts created with runbook; on-call can reproduce a simulated rollback in staging
E2E benchmark showing no more than 2% increase in average rollout time for quantized releases versus prior manual process
